questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the sum of the binary numbers $(101101101)_2$ and $(100011)_2$?
questions.solution:
Converting the given binary numbers to decimal:

$(101101101)_2 = 1 \times 2^8 + 0 \times 2^7 + 1 \times 2^6 + 1 \times 2^5 + 0 \times 2^4 + 1 \times 2^3 + 1 \times 2^2 + 0 \times 2^1 + 1 \times 2^0$

$(101101101)_2 = 256 + 0 + 64 + 32 + 0 + 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 365$

$(100011)_2 = 1 \times 2^5 + 0 \times 2^4 + 0 \times 2^3 + 0 \times 2^2 + 1 \times 2^1 + 1 \times 2^0$

$(100011)_2 = 32 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 35$

Adding the decimal values:

Sum $= 365 + 35 = 400$

Converting $400$ back to binary:

$400 = 256 + 128 + 16 = 2^8 + 2^7 + 2^4$

Therefore, $400 = (110010000)_2$

Answer: $(110010000)_2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $p = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} 2^j$ and $q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} 5^j$.

If $p + q = 15$, then what is $q - p$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} 2^j$ and $q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} 5^j$.

Simplifying $p$ and $q$:

$p = \sum_{j=1}^{n} j \log_{10} 2 = \log_{10} 2 \sum_{j=1}^{n} j = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} \log_{10} 2$

$q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} j \log_{10} 5 = \log_{10} 5 \sum_{j=1}^{n} j = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} \log_{10} 5$

Adding $p$ and $q$:

$p + q = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} (\log_{10} 2 + \log_{10} 5) = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} \log_{10} (2 \times 5) = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} \log_{10} 10$

Since $\log_{10} 10 = 1$, we get:

$p + q = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$

Given $p + q = 15$, we have:

$\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} = 15$

Now, finding $q - p$:

$q - p = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} \log_{10} 5 - \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} \log_{10} 2$

$q - p = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} (\log_{10} 5 - \log_{10} 2)$

$q - p = 15 \log_{10} \left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)$

$q - p = 15 \log_{10} 2.5$

questions.q: What is the number of solutions of $\log _4(x-1)=\log _2(x-3)$ ?
questions.solution:
$\log _4(x-1)=\log _2(x-3)\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{2} \log (x-1)=\log _2(x-3) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \log _2(x-1)=\log _2(x-3)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x-1=x^2-6 x+9 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x^2-7 x+10=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2-5 x-2 x+10=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x(x-5)-2(x-5)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad(x-5)(x-2)=0\end{aligned}\left[\begin{array}{l}x \neq 2 \text { because } \\ x-3 \gt 0, x \gt 3\end{array}\right]\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & x=2,5 \\
\Rightarrow & x=5
\end{array}$
Hence, one solution.

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text {  Since, } \frac{1!+3!+5!+7!+\ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots+199!}{24} \\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For $x \geq y \gt 1$, let $\log _x\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)+\log _y\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)=k$, then the value of $k$ can never be equal to:
questions.solution:
$\log _x\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)+\log _y\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)=k\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \log _x x-\log _x y+\log_e y-\log _y x=k \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1-\log _x y+1-\frac{1}{\log _x y}=k \\
& \text { Let, } \quad \log _x y=t \\
& \therefore \quad 2-t-\frac{1}{t}=k \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 t-t^2-1=k t \\
& \Rightarrow \quad t^2+(k-2) t+1=0 \\
& \text { For solution, } \quad \mathrm{D}=b^2-4 a c \geq 0 \\
& (k-2)^2-4 \geq 0 \quad(k-2)^2 \geq 0 \\
& k-2 \geq 2 \quad k-2 \leq 0 \\
& k \geq 4 \quad k \leq 0 \\
& \therefore k \geq 4 \text { or } k \leq 0
\end{aligned}$
Hence, $k \neq 1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $1-\log_{10}2=\log_{10}(5^x+4^x+3^x+2^x+1)$, then what is a value of $x$ ?
questions.solution:
The given equation is $1 - \log_{10}2 = \log_{10}(5^x + 4^x + 3^x + 2^x + 1)$

Simplifying the left hand side:

$1 - \log_{10}2 = \log_{10}10 - \log_{10}2 = \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{10}{2}\right) = \log_{10}5$

Equating this to the right hand side:

$\log_{10}5 = \log_{10}(5^x + 4^x + 3^x + 2^x + 1)$

Since the logarithmic function is one-to-one, we can equate the arguments:

$5 = 5^x + 4^x + 3^x + 2^x + 1$

$5^x + 4^x + 3^x + 2^x = 4$

Substituting $x = 0$ into the equation:

$5^0 + 4^0 + 3^0 + 2^0 = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4$

Thus, $x = 0$ satisfies the equation.

Answer: $0$

For the following two (02) items:
Let $p = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} 2^j$ and $q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} 5^j$.

If $p + q = 66$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} 2^j$ and $q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} 5^j$

Adding $p$ and $q$:

$p + q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} (\log_{10} 2^j + \log_{10} 5^j)$

$p + q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} (2^j \cdot 5^j)$

$p + q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \log_{10} (10^j)$

$p + q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} j \log_{10} 10$

Since $\log_{10} 10 = 1$, we get:

$p + q = \sum_{j=1}^{n} j = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$

Given $p + q = 66$:

$\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} = 66$

$n(n+1) = 132$

$n^2 + n - 132 = 0$

$(n - 11)(n + 12) = 0$

Since $n$ must be a positive integer, $n = 11$.

The value $n = 11$ satisfies the condition $9 \lt n \lt 12$.

Answer: $9 \lt n \lt 12$

questions.solution:
$|x-4|+|x-7|=15$
Case 1: $\quad x \lt 44-x+7-x=1511-2 x=152 x=-4x=-2 \Rightarrow$ One solution.
Case 2: $\quad 4 \leq x \lt 7x-4+7-x=15$ No solution
Case 3: $\quad x \geq 7x-4+x-7=152 x=26x=13 \Rightarrow$ One solution
$\therefore \quad$ Total 2 solutions; $x=-2,13$.

questions.q:
If $p^x = q^y = r^z$, where $x$, $y$ and $z$ are in GP, then consider the following statements:
I. $p$, $q$ and $r$ are in AP.
II. $\ln p$, $\ln q$ and $\ln r$ are in GP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Let $p^x = q^y = r^z = k$

Taking natural logarithm on all sides:

$x \ln p = y \ln q = z \ln r = \ln k$

$x = \dfrac{\ln k}{\ln p}$, $y = \dfrac{\ln k}{\ln q}$, $z = \dfrac{\ln k}{\ln r}$

Since $x$, $y$, and $z$ are in GP, $y^2 = xz$

Substituting the values of $x$, $y$, and $z$:

$\left( \dfrac{\ln k}{\ln q} \right)^2 = \left( \dfrac{\ln k}{\ln p} \right) \left( \dfrac{\ln k}{\ln r} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{(\ln q)^2} = \dfrac{1}{\ln p \ln r}$

$(\ln q)^2 = \ln p \ln r$

This implies that $\ln p$, $\ln q$, and $\ln r$ are in GP.

Statement II is correct, while Statement I is not necessarily true.

Answer: II only

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x^{\log } 7^x \gt 7$ where $x \gt 0$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
$x^{\log _7^x} \gt 7 ; x \gt 0$ taking log both sides $\Rightarrow \log _7^x \cdot \log x \gt \log 7\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{\log x}{\log 7} \cdot \log x \gt \log 7 \\ & \Rightarrow(\log x)^2 \gt (\log 7)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow(\log x)^2-(\log 7)^2 \gt 0 \\ & \Rightarrow(\log x+\log 7)(\log x-\log 7) \gt 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{7}, 7\end{aligned}$
$\therefore \quad x \in\left(0, \frac{1}{7}\right) \cup(7, \infty)$

questions.q: The mean weight of 150 students in a certain class is 60 kg . The mean weight of boys is 70 kg and that of girls is 55 kg . What are the number of boys and girls respectively in the class?
questions.solution:
Let no. of boys be $x$.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad 60=\frac{70 x+55(150-x)}{150} \\
& \Rightarrow 15 x+8250=9000 \\
& \Rightarrow 15 x=750 \\
& \Rightarrow x=50 \\
& \therefore \text { Boys }=50 \text { and girls }=100 .
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x+\log _{15}\left(1+3^x\right)=x \log _{15} 5+\log _{15} 12$, where $x$ is an integer, then what is $x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& x+\log _{15}\left(1+3^x\right)=x \log _{15} 5+\log _{15} 12 \\
& \Rightarrow x \cdot \log _{15} 15+\log _{15}\left(1+3^x\right)=x \log _{15} 5+\log _{15} 12 \\
& \left(\because \log _{15} 15=1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \log _{15} 15^x+\log _{15}\left(1+3^x\right)=\log _{15} 5^x+\log _{15} 12 \\
& \Rightarrow \log _{15} 15^x\left(1+3^x\right)=\log _{15}\left(5^x \times 12\right) \\
& (\because \log a+\log b=\log a b)
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad 15^x\left(1+3^x\right)=5^x \times 12 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3^x\left(1+3^x\right)=12 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3^x+3^{2 x}=12
\end{aligned}\mathrm{x}=1$ satisfies the above equation.

questions.q: If $x+\log _{10}\left(1+2^x\right)=x \log _{10} 5+\log _{10} 6$ then $x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & x+\log _{10}\left(1+2^x\right)=x \log _{10} 5+\log _{10} 6 \\ & \Rightarrow x-x \log _{10} 5=\log _{10} 6-\log _{10}\left(1+2^x\right) \\ & \Rightarrow x\left(1-\log _{10} 5\right)=\log _{10} 6-\log _{10}\left(1+2^x\right) \\ & \Rightarrow x\left(\log _{10} 10-\log _{10} 5\right)=\log _{10}\left(\frac{6}{1+2^x}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow x\left(\log _{10}\left(\frac{10}{5}\right)\right)=\log _{10}\left(\frac{6}{1+2^x}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow x \log _{10} 2=\log _{10}\left(\frac{6}{1+2^x}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $x y=4225$ where $x, y$ are natural numbers, then what is the minimum value of $x+y$ ?

Let $S=x+y=x+\frac{4225}{x}\frac{\mathrm{ds}}{\mathrm{dx}}=1-\frac{4225}{\mathrm{x}^2}=0\Rightarrow x=65\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{~s}}{\mathrm{dx}^2}=\frac{2.4225}{\mathrm{x}^3} \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{~d}^2 \mathrm{~s}}{\mathrm{dx}^2}\right)_{(\mathrm{x}=65)}=\frac{2.4225}{(65)^3} \gt 0\end{aligned}\therefore \quad x+y$ is minimum at $x=65$ and $y=65\therefore \quad$ Minimum value of $x+y=65+65=130$

questions.q:
If $A=\left\{x \in R: x^2+6 x-7 \lt 0\right\}$ and $B=\left\{x \in R: x^2+9 x+14 \gt 0\right\}$, then which of the following is/are correct?

$\begin{array}{lll}
x^2+6 x-7 \lt 0 & \& & x^2+9 x+14 \gt 0 \\
\Rightarrow(x-1)(x+7) \lt 0 & \& & \Rightarrow(x+2)(x+7) \gt 0 \\
\Rightarrow x \in(-7,1) & \& & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x} \in(-\infty,-7) \cup(-2, \infty)
\end{array}\therefore A \cap B=\{x \in R:-2 \lt x \lt 1\} \rightarrow$ It is true.
$A \backslash B=A-B=\{x \in R:-7 \lt x \lt -2\} \rightarrow$ It is also true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sum of all real roots of the equation $|\mathrm{x}-3|^2+|\mathrm{x}-3|-2=0$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & |\mathrm{x}-3|^2+|\mathrm{x}-3|-2=0 \\ & \text {Let }|\mathrm{x}-3|=\mathrm{t} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{t}^2+\mathrm{t}-2=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}^2+2 \mathrm{t}-\mathrm{t}-2=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}(\mathrm{t}+2)-1(\mathrm{t}+2)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(\mathrm{t}+2)(\mathrm{t}-1)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=-2 \text { or } \mathrm{t}=1\end{aligned}$
Since $t$ is modulus of a number, it cannot be negative.
$\begin{aligned}& \therefore \mathrm{t}=1 \Rightarrow|\mathrm{x}-3|=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}-3=1 \text { or } \mathrm{x}-3=-1 \\& \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=4 \text { or } 2
\end{aligned}$
Sum of roots $=4+2=6$.

questions.q: If $\log _a(a b)=x$, then what is $\log _b(a b)$ equal to?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $\left.A=\mid x \in R: x^2+6 x-7 \lt 0\right\}$ and $B=\left\{x \in R: x^2+9 x+14 \gt 0\right\}$, then which of the following is/ are correct?
1. $(A \cap B)=(-2,1)$
2. $(A / B)=(-7,-2)$
  
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}^2+6 \mathrm{x}-7 \lt 0 \\ & \Rightarrow(\mathrm{x}+7)(\mathrm{x}-1) \lt 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=(-7,1) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{A}=\{-6,-5,-4,-3,-2,-1,0\} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^2+9 \mathrm{x}+14 \gt 0 \\ & \Rightarrow(\mathrm{x}+7)(\mathrm{x}+2) \gt 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=(-\infty,-7) \cup(-2, \infty) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{R}-\{-7,-6,-5,-4,-3,-2\}\end{aligned}$
So $A \cap B=(-2,1)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\log _7 \log _7 \sqrt{7 \sqrt{7 \sqrt{7}}}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $\log _7 \log _7 \sqrt{7 \sqrt{7 \sqrt{7}}}=x$
then
$\begin{aligned}
7^x & =\log _7 \sqrt{7 \sqrt{7 \sqrt{7}}} \\
7^x & =\frac{1}{2} \cdot \log _7 7 \sqrt{7 \sqrt{7}} \\
7^x & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\log _7 7+\frac{1}{2} \log _7 7 \sqrt{7}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[1+\frac{1}{2} \log _7 7+\frac{1}{2} \log _7 \sqrt{7}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[1+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\right] \\
7^x & =\frac{7}{8} \\
x & =\log _7\left(\frac{7}{8}\right) \\
x & =\log _7 7-\log _7 8 \\
x & =1-3 \log _7 2
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $n=(2017)!$, then what is
$\frac{1}{\log _2 \mathrm{n}}+\frac{1}{\log _3 \mathrm{n}}+\frac{1}{\log _4 \mathrm{n}}+\ldots .+\frac{1}{\log _{2017} \mathrm{n}}$ equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{n}=(2017)! \\
& \frac{1}{\log _2 n}+\frac{1}{\log _3 n}+\frac{1}{\log _4 n}+\ldots .+\frac{1}{\log _{2017} n} \\
& =\frac{1}{\frac{\log n}{\log 2}}+\frac{1}{\frac{\log n}{\log 3}}+\frac{1}{\frac{\log n}{\log 4}}+\ldots .+\frac{1}{\frac{\log n}{\log 2017}} \\
& \left(\because \log _{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{~b}=\frac{\log _{\mathrm{b}}}{\log _{\mathrm{a}}}\right) \\
& =\frac{\log 2}{\log n}+\frac{\log 3}{\log n}+\frac{\log 4}{\log n}+\ldots .+\frac{\log 2017}{\log n} \\
& =\frac{\log 2+\log 3+\log 4+\ldots .+\log 2017}{\log n} \\
& =\frac{\log (2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4 \ldots 2017)}{\log _{\mathrm{n}}} \quad(\because \log a+\log b+\log c+\ldots \log (\text { a.b.c..... }) \\
& =\frac{\log (2017!)}{\log _{\mathrm{n}}}=\frac{\log _{\mathrm{n}}}{\log _{\mathrm{n}}}=1
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is $\frac{1}{\log _2 \mathrm{~N}}+\frac{1}{\log _3 \mathrm{~N}}+\frac{1}{\log _4 \mathrm{~N}}+\ldots .+\frac{1}{\log _{100} \mathrm{~N}}$ equal to $(\mathrm{N} \neq 1)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\log _2 \mathrm{~N}}+\frac{1}{\log _3 \mathrm{~N}}+\frac{1}{\log _4 \mathrm{~N}}+\ldots+\frac{1}{\log _{100} \mathrm{~N}} \\ & =\frac{\frac{1}{\log \mathrm{~N}}}{\log 2}+\frac{1}{\log \mathrm{~N}}+\frac{1}{\log 3}+\ldots+\frac{1}{\frac{\log \mathrm{~N}}{\log 4}} \\ & \quad\left(\because \log _{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{b}=\frac{\log \mathrm{b}}{\log \mathrm{N}}\right) \\ & =\frac{\log 2}{\log \mathrm{~N}}+\frac{\log 3}{\log \mathrm{~N}}+\frac{\log 4}{\log \mathrm{~N}}+\ldots .+\frac{\log 100}{\log \mathrm{~N}} \\ & =\frac{\log 2+\log 3+\log 4+\ldots .+\log 100}{\log \mathrm{~N}} \\ & =\frac{\log (2.3 .4 \ldots .100)}{\log \mathrm{N}}\end{aligned}=\frac{\log 100!}{\log \mathrm{N}}=\frac{1}{\frac{\log \mathrm{~N}}{\log 100!}}=\frac{1}{\log _{100!} \mathrm{N}}$

questions.q: If $\log _{10} 2, \log _{10}\left(2^x-1\right), \log _{10}\left(2^x+3\right)$ are in AP, then what is $x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \log _{10^2}, \log _{10}\left(2^x-1\right), \log _{10}\left(2^x+3\right) \text { are in A.P. } \\ & \therefore \log _{10}\left(2^x-1\right)=\log _{10} 2^2+\log _{10}\left(2^x+3\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \log _{10}\left(2^x-1\right)^2=\log _{10}\left(2^x+3\right) \\ & \Rightarrow\left(2^x-1\right)^2=2\left(2^x+3\right) \\ & \Rightarrow\left(2^x\right)^2-2.2^x+1=2.2^x+6 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(2^x\right)^2-4.2^x-5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(2^x-5\right)\left(2^x+1\right)=0 \\ & \therefore 2^x+1 \neq 0 \\ & \therefore 2^x-5=0 \\ & \therefore 2^x=5 \\ & \Rightarrow x=\log _2 5\end{aligned}$
